Article Title: Meta apologises for ‘error in restricting PM’s video’
Article Text:
The government says that the company admits lapses on child porn, deepfakes

Officials told Meta it could lose safe harbour status

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amid mounting scrutiny, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has apologised to the government for Facebook taking down PM Modi’s video, and the social media giant’s lapses related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deepfake content and errors in operating its platforms, government officials said. The tech major also confirmed that it took money to boost certain types of content, the officials added.Meta blamed technical glitches for Modi’s video being taken down, in which he had reached out to student protesters.“I apologised to the minister (Ashwini Vaishnaw) on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post,” Meta’s chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan said in a statement. Government officials said Zuckerberg’s apology was communicated through Kaplan.The apology came hours after Zuckerberg was given a three-day ultimatum by a parliamentary standing committee headed by BJP’s Nishikant Dubey on Wednesday to either apologise for taking down PM Modi’s video or lose the ‘safe harbour’ that protects Meta from any liability for the content posted on its platforms.The social media giant acknowledged during discussions with the government that significant sums had been paid for boosting certain categories of content and accepted that paid promotion had resulted in illegal content being amplified for specific audiences, officials said.The company expressed regret over the lapses and admitted mistakes in the way the platform had been operating, officials added.The meeting happened against the backdrop of widespread indignation in BJP and government quarters that Facebook facilitated algorithmic manipulation to fan discontent against the government over paper leaks and promote content, including a barrage of vile reels targeting the PM. Meta representatives will be summoned again, officials said, without disclosing the purpose or scope of the next meeting.Meta apologised for the shortcomings and assured authorities that corrective steps would be taken.Authorities also conveyed to Meta that it could not automatically claim protection available to intermediaries under Indian law if it actively selected who received content through algorithmic amplification or paid promotion. The company was told that such conduct could place it outside the definition of an intermediary, rendering it vulnerable to action by authorities and lawsuits by individuals.The government also sought details of safeguards to prevent the dissemination of CSAM, deepfakes and other harmful material. Officials said Meta accepted that illegal content had been promoted and acknowledged shortcomings in its systems.The government, meanwhile, is examining global regulatory approaches to children’s online safety as part of a broader review of its policy and legal framework. International models for protecting children online are being studied to assess whether additional safeguards or legislative changes are required as digital platforms come under increasing scrutiny over harmful and illegal content, it said in a statement.
Article Summary: The government says that the company admits lapses on child porn, deepfakes and errors in operating its platforms.officials told meta it could lose safe harbour status for the social media giant. The tech major also confirmed that it took money to boost certain types of content.

Article Title: Trai unveils draft service quality norms for network slicing
Article Text:
If cleared, telecom operators will be able to charge differently for different services like 4G and 5G, unlike now when both services have the same charge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Network slicing, which enables telecom service providers to provide different speeds of internet to different categories of consumers, could soon become a reality in India. Following a request from some large operators, the telecom department had asked Trai to examine this, and on Wednesday, the regulator issued a draft quality of service norms that factor in this controversial technology that some fear may affect net neutrality.The draft amendments to the Standards of Quality of Service of Access (Wireline and Wireless) and Broadband (Wireline and Wireless) Service Regulations, 2024, say: “...service provider must ensure that sufficient capacity is available in the network and shall submit the details, as per the format and manner prescribed by the authority, before launch of such network slicing.”The draft proposes to change the “typical download and upload speed offered to the subscribers” sentence in the existing rule with “technology-wise typical download and upload speed offered to subscribers for each tariff offering.” If cleared, telecom operators will be able to charge differently for different services like 4G and 5G, unlike now when both services have the same charge.
Article Summary: Network slicing enables telecom service providers to provide different speeds of internet to different categories of consumers. Following a request from some large operators, the telecom department had asked trai to examine this. On wednesday, the regulator issued a draft quality of service norms that factor in this technology.

Article Title: Navigation sat NVS-03 ready for launch, 3 more satellites to follow: Space min Jitendra Singh in LS
Article Text:
Noting the failure of replacement satellite NVS-02 in 2025, Jitendra Singh said that mecessary corrective measures have been incorporated

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The government is working to have the country’s Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System or NaVIC up and running again as it plans to launch four satellites in the near future.“NVS-03 is ready for launch after incorporation of all corrective measures arising from the NVS-02 anomaly. It will be followed by the launch of NVS-04 and NVS-05. One more satellite is planned thereafter to complete the seven-satellite NavIC base layer constellation,” space minister Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in Lok Sabha on Wednesday.He, however, did not mention the timeline for these launches.Noting the failure of replacement satellite NVS-02 in 2025, Jitendra Singh said, “Necessary corrective measures have been incorporated and successfully implemented and tested in CMS-03 satellite. The same will be followed in subsequent satellites, including the NavIC series of satellites carrying bi-propellant systems.”Currently, only IRNSS 1-B, IRNSS 1-L and NVS-01 are capable of providing navigation services. But for the NaVIC system to be operational effectively, at least four satellites with operational atomic clocks are required. So, NavIC is no longer providing standalone positioning services.In March this year, the last atomic clock on board Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System-1F (IRNSS-1F) stopped functioning, paralysing NavIC.The first-generation satellites for NavIC were launched between 2013 and 2018. However, the constellation of satellites soon began to face issues, with the atomic clocks on board several IRNSS series satellites repeatedly malfunctioning.The NVS series represents the second-generation satellites for NavIC. While Isro successfully placed NVS-01 in the desired orbit in 2023, the 2025 launch of NVS-02 failed. This has delayed the launch of NVS-03, NVS-04 and NVS-05.
Article Summary: The government is working to have the country’s indian regional navigational satellite system or navic up and running again. It plans to launch four satellites in the near future. Noting the failure of replacement satellite nvs-02 in 2025, jitendra singh said that mecessary corrective measures have been incorporated.

Article Title: 'Consumers paying more': Congress alleges E20 has tilted benefits towards ethanol producers
Article Text:
Centre reiterated E20 safe for vehicles, however Congress claims consumers are paying more than petrol

‘Low mileage due to E20, consumer paying more

NEW DELHI: Congress on Wednesday alleged that the Centre's push for E20 petrol has increased fuel costs for consumers while primarily benefiting ethanol producers, claiming that motorists are paying more despite assurances of cheaper fuel.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that since March 2025, regular fuel stations across the country have been supplying "practically only E20 petrol".Referring to earlier statements by Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, he said the government had claimed ethanol blending would bring the price of diesel down to Rs 50 per litre and provide a petrol alternative at Rs 55 per litre, but no such reduction had materialised.He further alleged that consumers are paying more due to the lower mileage of ethanol-blended fuel.“On the contrary, according to an independent analysis, between April 2023 and March 2026, consumers collectively spent an additional approximately ₹88,234 crore to compensate for the lower mileage from ethanol-blended fuel,” he wrote in X post.He further claimed that the Centre could have reduced the retail price of E20 petrol to offset the lower fuel efficiency and noted that the NITI Aayog's Ethanol Roadmap had recommended financial and tax incentives for E10 and E20 fuels to compensate consumers.Instead, the Congress leader alleged, the government approved subsidies of more than Rs 4,000 crore for ethanol producers, shifting the benefits of the programme towards industry rather than consumers."E20 has stripped the average middle-class Indian of options, imposed higher fuel costs on them, and placed an extra burden on the very vehicle they saved for years to buy. If any segment has benefited the most from E20, it is the ethanol producers," Ramesh said.However, the Centre has maintained that ethanol blending helps reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil, and supports farmers by creating demand.

Article Title: Apologise in 3 days or face action: Parliament panel to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg
Article Text:
Parliamentary standing committee demands apology from Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg over Facebook removing PM Modi's speech.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Parliamentary Standing Committee has asked Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg to issue an unconditional apology within three days over the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's speech from Facebook , warning that the company's safe-harbour immunity under the Information Technology Act could be withdrawn if it fails to do so.In a letter to electronics and information technology secretary S Krishnan, the Parliamentary standing committee on electronics and information technology, chaired by BJP MP Nishikant Dubey, said it had taken a "very serious" view of the removal of the PM Modi's video from Facebook for five to six hours."The removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video addressing students and Gen Z regarding examination controversies and strict actions against paper leaks from Facebook for 5-6 hours viewed very seriously by the Committee," the letter signed by A Jyothirmayi said.The panel said Zuckerberg must tender an unconditional apology within three days of receiving the letter. Failing that, it recommended that Meta's safe-harbour immunity under Section 79(3) of the Information Technology Act be withdrawn and that action be initiated against the company as a publisher.The committee also called for stricter action against intermediary platforms that host child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and content demeaning women.It said platforms that fail to remove such content should face action under Section 79(3) of the IT Act.Meanwhile, Meta team led by its chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan, met MeitY secretary S Krishnan. The meeting lasted around 45 minutes, during which Meta officials explained the reasons behind the erroneous takedown of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video.Separately, the panel urged the Government of India to initiate action against the head of Google India in connection with an alleged cyber fraud case being investigated by Hyderabad Police, in which investors reportedly lost more than Rs 48 lakh through fraudulent investment applications."The Committee while discussing Hyderabad Cyber Police Action against the Google India Head as a co-accused along with the Cyber fraudsters after the complainants alleged that they lost more than Rs.48 lakhs by investing through fraud Apps, the Committee desired that similar action be taken against the Google India by the Government of India," the letter stated.
Article Summary: Parliamentary standing committee demands apology from meta chief mark zuckerberg over facebook removing pm modi's speech. The panel said zuckerberg must tender an unconditional apology within three days of receiving the letter. Failing that, it recommended that meta's safe-harbour immunity under section 79(3) of the information technology act be withdrawn.

Article Title: Govt dismisses reports of fuel quality issues, says checks on
Article Text:

Poll Vote & Share your view How confident are you in the quality checks conducted by oil marketing companies on fuel? Very confident Somewhat confident Not confident Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Dismissing reports of fuel quality issues at outlets, govt Tuesday said additional checks have been introduced by oil marketing companies (OMCs) to detect fuel contamination and adulteration.In a post on X, the petroleum ministry said OMCs were regularly monitoring fuel quality, water ingress and contamination, and that only two cases of chloride contamination had been detected so far."In addition to the advanced and elaborate testing protocols already in place, further checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing 8-12 times a day at over 87,000 outlets. Over 2,000 samples have also been tested for chloride/sulphide. Only two cases of chloride contamination have been found in the entire country till now, and sales from those pumps were suspended immediately," ministry said.It added that oil companies had been instructed to take proactive steps to detect any possible contamination across the fuel supply chain, and strict action would be taken if contamination or adulteration was found at any retail outlet.Through a series of infographics on X, ministry said there was "zero compromise" on quality benchmarks and that 302 tankers carrying 10,500 kilolitres of ethanol were rejected between July 2024 and June 2026 for failing quality standards.It added that ethanol used for blending must comply with BIS IS 15464, have a minimum purity of 99.6% and be accompanied by a certified quality report. The ministry said ethanol is stored in dedicated facilities to prevent contamination, its quality is monitored regularly to ensure consistency and every tanker is sampled from both the top and bottom before being accepted.Separately, govt has so far approved Rs 4,687 crore as interest subsidy for eligible ethanol projects under its various support schemes, minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi told Parliament Monday. Under the schemes, govt bears an interest subvention of 6% or 50% of the interest rate charged by lenders, whichever is lower, for five years on loans taken to set up new distilleries or expand existing ethanol production capacity.
Article Summary: Govt dismisses reports of fuel quality issues at outlets. Omcs regularly monitoring fuel quality, water ingress and contamination. Only two cases of chloride contamination had been detected so far. 302 tankers carrying 10,500 kilolitres of ethanol rejected for failing quality standards.

Article Title: Consumers already bearing UPI costs through broader economy: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra
Article Text:
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra gestures on MPC policy

NEW DELHI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said consumers already bear the cost of UPI transactions indirectly even if merchant fees are not explicitly charged.Responding to questions on enabling merchant fees on UPI, Malhotra said it was too early to take a view and the focus remains on strengthening the payments infrastructure. “it is very premature right now. Now, costs have to be paid by someone — it's a public [good]; we all want this particular infrastructure to continue to strengthen, become more efficient. That's our focus as of now — let's watch how developments proceed,” he said.Government has proposed amendments to the law that barred any form of merchant fees on UPI transactions. There have also been reports that the government plans to allow merchant fees to be charged on UPI transactions with value of over Rs 2,000. The absence of fees has resulted in banks ceding the payments as a service space to fintechs with PhonePe and Google Pay being an almost duopoly using the transactions to draw more users to their platform where they seek to earn revenue through distribution of other services.Malhotra said the objective is to scale up UPI usage significantly and any decision on fees must consider its impact on adoption. “The goal is to have 800 million transactions a day or so. So, imposing a fee ...let's wait, it's premature right now. But please keep in mind that ultimately it is the consumer, in some way or the other, who is already paying it — it may not be the same consumer, it may be the general economy, and you don't get to see it directly, but it's already happening in some form,” he said.He said the priority is to ensure sustained investment in UPI and the availability of revenue streams to support its growth.
Article Summary: Government has proposed amendments to the law that barred any form of merchant fees on upi transactions. Malhotra said it was too early to take a view and the focus remains on strengthening the payments infrastructure. The absence of fees has resulted in banks ceding the payments as a service space to fintechs.

Article Title: Once owned by Bill Gates, this $650 million hydrogen superyacht sparked online protests after a loud party disturbed an Italian village
Article Text:
Why Bill Gates' superyacht was built for silence

How a quiet yacht became the centre of a noise controversy

What makes Breakthrough different from other superyachts



How the hydrogen-powered system works

Why Breakthrough is considered an engineering milestone









One of the world's most exclusive charter yachts

A silent revolution with an unexpected ending



A superyacht designed to redefine luxury through silence and sustainability has unexpectedly found itself at the centre of a noise controversy. The 390-foot (119-metre) hydrogen-powered Breakthrough, originally commissioned for Bill Gates before being sold to Canadian billionaire Patrick Dovigi, reportedly sparked online complaints after an onboard party disturbed residents of a quiet Italian village. Anchored off Scaglieri Beach on Elba Island in late July, music from the gathering was said to have carried across the bay, prompting criticism on social media. Although authorities reported no fines or official investigation, the incident drew attention because one of the world's quietest yachts made headlines for all the wrong reasons.Breakthrough was conceived as a technological milestone in sustainable luxury yachting. Built by Dutch shipbuilder Feadship, the vessel was designed to minimise both emissions and noise through an advanced hydrogen fuel-cell system and electric pod propulsion. Unlike conventional superyachts, it eliminates many of the mechanical components responsible for vibration and underwater noise, making it one of the quietest yachts ever constructed.Although the yacht was originally commissioned for Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, he never took ownership.Before delivery, it was purchased by Canadian billionaire Patrick Dovigi, founder and CEO of GFL Environmental.According to Italian newspaper La Nazione, Breakthrough arrived off Scaglieri Beach on July 27 alongside its 52-foot support vessel, Breakthrough II. That evening, guests reportedly attended a private party while the yacht remained anchored in the Gulf of Biodola.Residents and holidaymakers claimed the music echoed across the bay, disturbing the normally peaceful surroundings and prompting several complaints on social media. Despite the criticism, there were no reports of intervention by the police or Coast Guard, and no formal investigation into noise levels was announced.Measuring 390 feet in length, Breakthrough is regarded as the world's first hydrogen fuel-cell superyacht. It combines luxury with advanced environmental technology, making it one of the most innovative vessels ever built.The yacht stores around four tonnes of liquid hydrogen inside a 92-cubic-metre cryogenic tank maintained at approximately minus 253 degrees Celsius. Sixteen hydrogen fuel cells generate about three megawatts of electricity by combining hydrogen with oxygen, producing electricity, water and usable heat instead of conventional exhaust emissions.The hydrogen fuel cells primarily supply electricity for the yacht's extensive onboard facilities, including air conditioning, lighting, kitchens, swimming pools and entertainment systems. According to Feadship, these hotel services account for the majority of a superyacht's annual energy consumption.The hydrogen system can keep these facilities operating for nearly a week while the yacht is anchored without relying on conventional generators. For longer voyages, Breakthrough also uses MTU generators capable of running on hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) biofuel, giving it both long-range capability and lower emissions.Traditional superyachts rely on shaft-driven propulsion systems that generate vibration and underwater noise. Breakthrough instead uses electric pod propulsion, reducing mechanical movement and creating a much quieter experience for passengers while also lowering underwater sound that can affect marine life.Its combination of hydrogen fuel cells, electric propulsion and hybrid biofuel technology has made it one of the most significant engineering achievements in the modern superyacht industry.Although Breakthrough has attracted global attention, hydrogen-powered superyachts are still exceptionally uncommon. Liquid hydrogen has a far lower energy density by volume than conventional marine fuels, meaning it requires much larger, heavily insulated cryogenic storage tanks kept at around −253°C. Refuelling infrastructure is also limited, with only a handful of ports worldwide currently capable of handling liquid hydrogen safely. These challenges have slowed widespread adoption despite growing interest in low-emission marine propulsion.Today, Breakthrough commands an estimated charter rate of around $4 million per week, making it one of the most expensive yachts available for hire. Its size, hydrogen technology and luxury amenities place it among the most advanced superyachts ever built.While the vessel represents a major step forward in cleaner marine technology, its recent appearance off Italy's coast has shown that even groundbreaking engineering cannot prevent a celebration onboard from becoming international news.Breakthrough was built to demonstrate that the future of luxury yachting could be cleaner, quieter and more environmentally responsible. Its hydrogen fuel-cell technology remains a landmark achievement in marine engineering. Yet its latest headlines serve as a reminder that even the world's quietest superyacht can become the loudest story when the people aboard make more noise than the engines ever could.
Article Summary: The 390-foot (119-metre) hydrogen-powered breakthrough was originally commissioned for bill gates before being sold to canadian billionaire patrick dovigi. Residents and holidaymakers claimed the music echoed across the bay, disturbing the normally peaceful surroundings.

Article Title: Elon Musk is not pleased with Zohran Mamdani's grocery stores idea, calls him 'a thief and a liar, plain and simple'
Article Text:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani

What Elon Musk said about Zohran Mamdani's grocery store plan



What is Zohran Mamdani's grocery store plan

Critics question how New York will fund lower grocery prices

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has sharply criticised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani over his plan to open city-backed grocery stores that promise to sell some everyday food items at prices below traditional retailers. Responding to a post on X (formerly Twitter) that questioned how the proposed stores would operate, Elon Musk dismissed the plan and accused Mamdani of misleading New Yorkers. “Mamdani is a thief and a liar, plain and simple,” Musk wrote in the post. The billionaire also argued that advances in AI and robotics, rather than government-backed programmes, would eventually make goods and services much cheaper or even free.Elon Musk made the comments while responding to an X post by user @jason, who criticised the economics behind Mamdani's proposal. The user argued that grocery businesses typically operate on very small profit margins and questioned the city's plan to seek private operators to run the stores.Responding to the post, Elon Musk wrote: “What they’re doing won’t matter.” He then suggested that AI and robots could eventually transform the cost of producing and delivering goods and services.“AI & robots will actually deliver the free goods & services that those thieves pretend to offer, while actually stealing from others,” Musk said.“Mamdani is a thief and a liar, plain and simple,” he added.Zohran Mamdani's administration has proposed opening five city-backed grocery stores, with one planned for each of New York City's five boroughs. The city has allocated $70 million in capital funding for the programme. The first store is expected to open in Hunts Point in the Bronx by the end of 2027, followed by locations in East Harlem, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island.Under the proposal, private grocery operators would handle day-to-day operations, including staffing, sourcing products and merchandising. The city would provide locations, cover major occupancy costs and set pricing and operating requirements.Mamdani's administration says shoppers could save about 30% on a core basket of groceries. It estimates that the programme could save an average New Yorker about $90 a month, or roughly $1,000 a year.The basket is expected to include fresh produce, meat and seafood as well as around 20 categories covering pantry staples, dairy and refrigerated products. Prices for these products would be locked monthly instead of changing week to week.The proposal has drawn criticism from economists, political commentators and business groups who question how the city can offer discounts of around 30% when grocery stores generally operate on thin profit margins. Critics argue that taxpayers could ultimately bear part of the cost through public funding, waived rent on government-owned properties and other support.They have also warned that publicly backed stores could put private supermarkets, bodegas and other small grocery businesses at a disadvantage because those businesses must pay expenses such as rent and property taxes themselves.Mamdani's administration, however, argues that removing some of those major operating costs is precisely what will allow the city-backed stores to offer lower prices. The plan comes as New Yorkers continue to face grocery prices that remain substantially higher than they were before the Covid-19 pandemic.
Article Summary: New york mayor zohran mamdani has proposed opening five city-backed grocery stores, with one planned for each of new york city's five boroughs. The first store is expected to open in hunts point in the bronx by the end of 2027, followed by locations in east harlem, brooklyn, queens and staten island.

Article Title: After 27 years and 18 desk moves, Jeff Dean is leaving Google; His ‘goodbye email’ explains why
Article Text:
Jeff Dean, Google's 30th employee and chief scientist, is leaving after 27 years to lead AI startup Discovery Loop.

What Jeff Dean built at Google, and what he wants to build next

Jeff Dean's goodbye email to Google, in full

Subject: Thank you and farewell

Hi everyone,

It has been an absolute pleasure to work with you and to help build some of the most widely used and impactful products of all time. As a kid, I dreamed of helping build software that would be used by many people, and Google now has thirteen products used by more than a billion people (amazing!). Our work has had a tremendous impact in the world, and I have been lucky enough to collaborate and form friendships with many colleagues whom I deeply admire, respect, and enjoy.

It still brings me joy every time I see people out in the world using our products to find information, handle email, translate something, watch videos, learn new things, navigate and understand the physical world, browse the web, use their phone, run large-scale computations on our infrastructure, ride in an autonomous vehicle, or perform complex tasks with the help of our AI systems. I hope you all share this sense of joy, because it is a shared accomplishment!

My longtime friends and collaborators Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le and I have been excitedly discussing how AI can help discover new things with the right kinds of automated loops.

It's a big step, but we've decided to leave Google to co-found Discovery Loop, a new public benefit corporation whose mission is to automate machine learning, science, and engineering to accelerate discoveries and progress.

Ambitious as it sounds, we believe this approach can make meaningful progress against many of the NAE Grand Challenge problems (nae.edu/20782/grand-challenges-project), and we are excited about trying something new, in a smaller setting. Sundar and Alphabet have been very understanding and are helping to support us along with outside investors. We leave with the belief that Google and Gemini are extremely well positioned for amazing impact in the future and we will all be cheering you on from outside!

I have deeply enjoyed collaborating and starting many different kinds of projects here over the last 27 years, and I will miss many aspects of this. Some of the projects and memories I will cherish include:

Working on multiple generations of Google Search as we increased our index size 100X, our queries served / sec 1000X, and our update frequency for the index by 10,000X over a few-year period

Creating the first Google Ads system and later creating and launching Google Content Ads

Helping to launch Google News and Google Translate

Working on infrastructure like MapReduce, BigTable, Spanner, DistBelief, TensorFlow, and Pathways with an awesome set of people

Starting the TPU program and working on other exciting hardware projects with talented colleagues

Doing research with many others on unsupervised learning, model distillation, mixture-of-experts model architectures, word2vec, neural architecture search, RL for ASIC design, AI for health care, and working on multiple generations of Large Language Models (LLMs)

Seeing the awesome work that people in Google Brain and Google Research did over many years when I was lucky enough to manage these organizations

Starting the Gemini effort with Oriol Vinyals as co-tech-leads and working with an amazing team on multiple generations of Gemini and Gemma

Biking to offsites in Monterey

The "Run or Else…" group runs over the last few years

Changing offices 18 times, and visiting 29 Google offices across five continents (did you know that with a Google badge, you can make a cappuccino in more than 100 cities around the world?)

Most importantly, feeling lucky and inspired getting to work amongst such a wonderful and talented group of colleagues

To the many, many people with whom I have worked over the years, I apologize for this impersonal email rather than a face-to-face chat: I didn't want you all to find out through second- or third-hand gossip and it was impractical to tell everyone in a more personal way all at once.

I will be at Google through tomorrow, August 6th. If you're in Mountain View and are so inclined, please stop by my desk and say goodbye in person tomorrow, or drop me a reply to this email. There will be a [remainder redacted in the shared screenshot]

All the best!

-Jeff

Jeff Dean's farewell note to Google runs long, and the most telling part isn't about AI at all. It's a list. Wedged between scaling Google Search's index 100X and starting the TPU program, he mentions biking to offsites in Monterey, a group run called "Run or Else…", changing offices 18 times, and the fact that a Google badge gets you a cappuccino in more than 100 cities. Twenty-seven years, reduced to bullet points he clearly enjoyed writing.The news underneath the nostalgia: Thursday, August 6 is his last day. Dean, chief scientist at Google DeepMind and one of the very few engineers whose work touches nearly every layer of Google's stack, is leaving to co-found Discovery Loop, a public benefit corporation, with Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le. He joined in 1999, when the company had 25 employees. He leaves it at 190,000-plus.CEO Sundar Pichai 's send-off for Jeff Dean drew the same arc: over 27 years, he said, Dean and Ghemawat drove some of Google's most significant technology transitions, from its early search infrastructure to the neural networks that built the modern AI era. "On a personal note, it's been a privilege to work alongside Jeff and Sanjay," Pichai wrote, adding that Google will keep collaborating with the new startup as a founding investor and Cloud partner.Dean’s résumé is most of modern Google. He wrote the first Ads system, helped launch News and Translate, and with Ghemawat designed MapReduce, BigTable and Spanner—systems that became the template for how Amazon and Meta handled global traffic. The two are the only Google employees ever named senior fellow, the company's highest technical honour. Then came 2011 and Google Brain, the research lab Dean built that pushed the entire industry toward AI. Its early hires included Le and Vinyals, the same two men now following him out.That's the quiet irony here. Brain's researchers helped pioneer the technology behind today's chatbots, and Google was slow to act on it. After ChatGPT landed in late 2022, the company folded Brain into DeepMind, and Dean and Vinyals were put on Gemini. His profile inside Google appeared to shrink as Sergey Brin returned and took hold of the AI push.Discovery Loop is an attempt to skip the bureaucracy entirely. The four want to build AI that improves itself with little human input—recursive self-improvement—then point the same machinery at chip design, drug discovery and materials science. Dean's argument is that the experimental loop has always been human-intensive and doesn't have to be. Seed funding comes from Radical Ventures, Khosla Ventures and Alphabet itself, which has also agreed to supply compute for at least a year. It's structured as a public benefit corporation, like Anthropic and OpenAI, and Dean says it may make calls that aren't in the company's purest financial interests.The note ends with an apology for being an email. He didn't want people hearing it as second-hand gossip, he writes, and invites anyone in Mountain View to stop by his desk. That's the tell. A man who spent 27 years building systems for a billion users at a time signed off worrying about how a few thousand colleagues would find out.
Article Summary: Jeff dean, google's 30th employee and chief scientist, is leaving after 27 years to lead ai startup discovery loop. Dean: "it has been an absolute pleasure to work with you and to help build some of the most widely used and impactful products of all time" jeff dean, chief scientist at google deepmind, is leaving to co-found discovery loop.

Article Title: After telling employees to stop using Claude Code, Microsoft's internal memo has more 'bad news' for Anthropic
Article Text:
Microsoft's new internal memo makes OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default model for its engineers, replacing a setup that had been quietly routing GitHub Copilot work to Anthropic's Claude.

GitHub Copilot's auto-router was quietly sending Microsoft engineers to Claude

Microsoft's AI token budget targets now put a ceiling on every division

Anthropic keeps its Microsoft deals but loses the GitHub Copilot default

Microsoft spent May telling its Windows, Office and Surface engineers to wind down Claude Code and move to GitHub Copilot CLI before the fiscal year closed on June 30. That looked like a licensing decision, and an expensive one for Anthropic. This week's internal memo suggests the harder blow was still coming.Jay Parikh, the executive vice president who runs Microsoft's CoreAI organisation, wrote to his teams that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for," asked engineers to review their own AI spending, and made OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default model for internal use. 404 Media first reported the memo, which lands at a company that has just posted another record quarter and is still worried enough about its own AI bill to put a ceiling on it.The default-model line is the part Anthropic will feel. According to reporting by Alex Heath, Microsoft's internal GitHub Copilot configuration previously ran on an auto-router that leaned mostly on Anthropic's models. In practice, thousands of Microsoft engineers were writing code with Claude tokens without ever choosing Claude, and Microsoft was paying for it. Cancelling Claude Code took away a product people had asked for.Changing the router takes away the traffic nobody had to ask for.Parikh framed it as efficiency rather than divorce. Shifting more workloads to OpenAI models, he wrote, helps the company get greater value from its token investment. He also stressed that Microsoft is not chasing lower usage: "We are not optimizing for fewer tokens. We are optimizing for more impact per token."Since July, every Microsoft division has carried an AI token budget target, and employees can look up their individual spend on an internal dashboard. The guidelines seen by 404 Media note that many engineers were burning through anywhere from a few hundred to a few thousand dollars in tokens each month.Microsoft is late to this. Uber's engineering organisation exhausted its entire planned 2026 AI coding budget in four months. Satya Nadella himself admitted at a live Hard Fork taping in June that plenty of tokenmaxxing was happening inside Microsoft, called the habit addictive, then delivered the line that now reads like policy: don't use frontier models for non-frontier problems.None of this ends the relationship. Claude models remain reachable through Copilot CLI, Microsoft Foundry customers still get Sonnet, Opus and Haiku under the November deal, and Microsoft has continued to favour Anthropic inside Microsoft 365 Copilot for tasks where it outperforms OpenAI. Microsoft even worked with Anthropic to bring Claude Cowork technology into Microsoft 365 Copilot.But defaults are where volume lives. Anthropic's business has been built substantially on enterprise coding workloads, and its largest customer just rewired its internal plumbing to send those workloads elsewhere by default. Rajesh Jha's May memo said Copilot CLI gave Microsoft a product it could shape directly with GitHub. Parikh's memo explains the other half of that sentence. Microsoft wanted a tool it controlled, and a bill it could predict, and Claude was expensive on both counts.
Article Summary: Microsoft makes openai's gpt-5.6 the default model for its engineers. That replaces a setup that had been quietly routing github copilot work to anthropic's claude. Microsoft spent may telling its windows, office and surface engineers to wind down claude code.

Article Title: UltraProlink launches Snap-Z, a DSLR-style magnetic smartphone grip
Article Text: Home-grown consumer tech brand UltraProlink has launched the Snap-Z Grip, a compact magnetic smartphone camera grip with a DSLR camera style magnetic grip. In a press release, the company said that the gadget is designed for content creators, travellers, vloggers. It combines an ergonomic grip, intuitive traditional-style controls, a Mag-Safe-style magnetic attachment and a detachable Bluetooth shutter. The UltraProlink Snap-Z Grip is available for Rs 1,999 on UltraProlink.com and Amazon.in.“The thoughtful design helps reduce hand fatigue while improving stability for reels, travel videos, product photography and everyday shooting in both portrait and landscape orientations,” the company said.The Snap-Z comes with a Mag-Safe-style magnetic mount that snaps securely onto compatible iPhones and magnetic cases. The magnetic metal ring included in the box extends compatibility to Android smartphones and other non-magnetic devices. This makes the Grip a versatile accessory that works with almost any smartphone.The firm also has provided a metal ring in the box for non-magnetic phones. Its detachable Bluetooth shutter functions as a tactile camera button while attached to the grip and doubles as a wireless remote with a range of up to 10m, ideal for selfies, group photos, tripod shots and hands-free videos.It pairs instantly with both Android and iPhone devices and works directly with the native camera app without requiring any additional software.The grip features one-handed controls with a responsive shutter button, zoom toggle and mode-switching support. The grip weighs 109g and can slip easily into a pocket, sling bag or backpack. Its dual-sided magnetic design also supports compatible accessories such as ring lights, to expand your mobile shooting setup with ease.Commenting on the launch, Pankaj Mirchandani, Founder & CEO, UltraProlink said: “Smartphones are the world’s most-used cameras, but holding one steady shouldn’t be this hard. UltraProlink’s Snap-Z Grip is a single compact accessory that brings the comfort of a DSLR-like ergonomic grip to every smartphone. It makes every shot possible with one hand, feel steadier, more comfortable and more enjoyable”
Article Summary: The snap-z comes with a mag-safe-style magnetic mount that snaps securely onto compatible iphones and magnetic cases. The grip features one-handed controls with a responsive shutter button, zoom toggle and mode-switching support. Its detachable bluetooth shutter functions as a tactile camera button while attached to the grip and doubles as a wireless remote.

Article Title: Microsoft retires 8-year-old employee tool, here's the message HR shared on its shutting down
Article Text:
Microsoft retires 8-year-old employee tool: Transition timeline



Performance review overhaul at Microsoft



Microsoft's first-ever voluntary retirement offer for 8,500-plus US employees



Microsoft is retiring Perspectives, its peer-feedback tool which the employees have used since 2018 to request peer feedback on their performance, according to an internal message reviewed by Business Insider. The retirement of the tool comes as the company is reworking on the broader approach to performance management. “The Perspectives tool is being retired,” the HR message stated. “Feedback remains an important part of our growth mindset, and we heard from employees and managers that feedback is most valuable when shared through ongoing, in-the-moment conversations rather than formal requests.”For those unaware, the Perspectives tool allowed employees solicit input on their work directly from colleagues, with responses visible to both the employee and their manager. Microsoft designed the tool to make asking for feedback feel routine and low-pressure rather than something tied to formal review cycles.The shutdown isn't immediate. Employees can no longer initiate new feedback requests through the tool, but they can still respond to requests already in progress and export their feedback history up until September 15, per the internal communication.The retirement of Perspectives comes as Microsoft simplifies its performance review system, moving to five rating categories and sharpening distinctions in employee performance.Managers have also been instructed to reduce the number of employees in higher-level engineering roles, part of a broader flattening of the organization that reflects Big Tech’s shift toward a more demanding work culture.That combination — fewer senior roles, sharper performance grading, and the removal of an informal peer-feedback channel — fits into what's been described as a broader shift toward a more intense work culture across large tech companies in recent years, a trend that has touched firms beyond Microsoft as well.In related news, in May this year, Microsoft announced its first-ever voluntary retirement offer for 8,500-plus US employees. the package combines healthcare coverage, cash severance, and a partial stock vesting bump for long-serving US employees who decide to walk away. About 7 percent of Microsoft's US workforce, or roughly 8,750 people, are eligible. The formula is simple: add your age to your years of service, and if the total is 70 or more, the offer is on the table. Employees get 30 days to decide.The medical side of the package is the headline benefit for anyone retiring before they hit Medicare age. Microsoft is offering five years of medical, dental, vision, and well-being coverage. The first year is fully subsidised by the company. For the remaining four, employees will pay a monthly premium themselves. That distinction matters. A 55-year-old walking out today still has a decade before Medicare kicks in at 65, and the cost of bridging that gap will land squarely on whatever Microsoft decides to charge for those four out-years.
Article Summary: Microsoft retires 8-year-old employee tool: transition timeline.performance review overhaul at microsoft also underway. Microsoft's first-ever voluntary retirement offer for 8,500-plus us employees is on the table for employees who are 70 and older.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.
